part_title: Secure Data Engineering, Identity and Recoverability

scenes.title: Secure Data Engineering: Quality and Privacy
scenes.narration: Start at the three data sources: S3 files, RDS application records and Kinesis event streams. The next panel uses AWS Glue Data Quality to assess completeness, accuracy, timeliness and consistency; these are different checks, so a recent record may still be wrong or incomplete. Follow the arrow into lineage: the pictured Amazon DataZone capability helps users understand where supported data came from and how it moved through preparation steps. Then protect sensitive fields before the data reaches SageMaker. Masking obscures values, tokenization substitutes surrogate tokens, and encryption protects data at rest or in transit; tokenization does not necessarily preserve the original data format. In the customer-support example below, profile missing labels and invalid formats, document the transformations, protect personal names and email addresses, then train with reviewed data. Good model quality and privacy are joint requirements. A cleaned dataset can still expose personal information if masking and access controls are skipped.

scenes.title: Secure Data Access and Integrity
scenes.narration: Read the large center architecture as two distinct access paths. Human staff sign in through IAM Identity Center using single sign-on and multi-factor authentication, then receive task-appropriate AWS roles or permissions. Applications and jobs do not use a human login session: they use dedicated IAM roles with least privilege. Both paths lead to approved stores such as S3 training data or DynamoDB application records. The lower boxes add logging and monitoring. CloudTrail records relevant AWS API activity, but object-level S3 data events and other supported data events need to be explicitly enabled when required; CloudWatch helps surface alarms and operational signals. On the right, integrity is broader than access control. Check for unexpected changes using validation or checksums, keep appropriate backups with AWS Backup, and test recovery rather than assuming a backup always restores. The example grants data scientists only the S3 actions they need. Security means authorized access, a trace of changes and recoverable accurate data.
